findings.source_passage: frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon
findings.source_locator: preamble, after 'Most of the confidences were unsought—'
findings.why_it_matters: This sardonic aside is a prime example of Nick’s self-ironizing voice; stripping it flattens the ethical frame the novel opens with.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the entire clause verbatim or keep its triple-gesture rhythm intact.

findings.source_passage: There was so much to read, for one thing, and so much fine health to be pulled down out of the young breath-giving air.
findings.why_it_matters: The lush cadence here crystallises Nick’s hopeful mood; its removal dulls the seasonal rebirth motif that critics repeatedly cite.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the sentence unchanged; if compressing, preserve the ‘fine health … breath-giving air’ phrasing.

findings.source_passage: They are not perfect ovals—like the egg in the Columbus story, they are both crushed flat at the contact end—
findings.why_it_matters: The Columbus-story parenthetical is a textbook example of Fitzgerald’s whimsical geography; deleting it erases a frequently annotated stylistic flourish.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full parenthetical so the comic comparison survives.

findings.source_passage: Slenderly, languidly, their hands set lightly on their hips, the two young women preceded us out on to a rosy-coloured porch
findings.source_locator: transition to dinner, just before candle dialogue
findings.why_it_matters: The balletic adverbs and posture details are key to the ethereal portrait of Daisy and Jordan; losing them bleaches the scene’s visual signature.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the sentence intact or replicate its triple-adverb glide and hip-set image.

findings.source_passage: “We’ve got to beat them down,” whispered Daisy, winking ferociously toward the fervent sun.
findings.source_locator: Goddard race rant, after Tom’s Nordic speech
findings.why_it_matters: Daisy’s sardonic collusion undercuts Tom’s rant and complicates her character; excising it blunts the novel’s treatment of racial ideology.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert Daisy’s mocking line to preserve the ironic counterpoint.

summary: Five mid-level signature and voice passages have been cut or flattened; restore them.
